openItems.explanation: The 3rd installment is $3,905.90 short since September 15, 2026 even with the annualized method and the June payment counted. The penalty runs at 7% (about $0.75 a day): $39.71 to November 7, $44.20 if the catch-up settles November 13. It cannot be removed for reasonable cause; paying now is the only way to stop it. A person schedules the payment.

The June 15 payment of $12,075.00 (EFT 270496102284) was designated to tax period 12/2025, the 2025 year, which was already paid in full. Left there, it is a 2025 overpayment, not a 2026 installment: the 2nd installment would have been $1,121.40 short from June 15, the 3rd $15,980.90 short now, and the penalty so far $181.73. A person (with Form 2848 on file, or the controller) asks the IRS to move it to 12/2026. If it is not moved before December 15, pay another $12,075.00 then and claim the 2025 overpayment back.

The annualized method rests on the controller's closed-month taxable income for 3, 6 and 9 months ($31,420.00, $139,860.00, $248,610.00), not reviewed. The first quarter includes the $30,000.00 officer bonus paid January 9, which annualizing multiplies by 4; a person confirms the interim figures and that no item is an extraordinary item the Form 2220 instructions add after annualizing. Form 2220 with Schedule A must be attached to the 2026 return.

The safe harbor is the $59,302.33 of tax on the 2025 return filed October 13, 2026, the Form 1120 demo's figure. The 2025 draft left officer pay approval and the related-party advance open; an amended 2025 return filed before December 15 would reset the 4th installment's base. A person confirms no amendment is planned before then.

Unsigned plan. Nothing has been paid or scheduled: $3,905.90 on November 13 and $15,246.43 on December 15, both EFTPS, Form 1120, tax period 12/2026, estimated tax. Paying only the safe harbor leaves about $13,542.47 due April 15, 2027 on the projected tax of $72,844.80; the controller may prefer to pay more in December for cash planning. The projection changes with the December results.

rules.question: What must HANGS pay in 2026 to avoid the estimated tax penalty?
rules.whyItMatters: Each installment is 25% of the required annual payment: the lesser of this year's tax or last year's tax, if last year was a full 12-month year with tax on the return.
rules.effective: 26 U.S.C. 6655(d) as published by Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute.
rules.excerpt: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amount of any required installment shall be 25 percent of the required annual payment. ... the lesser of (i) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return for the taxable year ..., or (ii) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return of the corporation for the preceding taxable year. Clause (ii) shall not apply if the preceding taxable year was not a taxable year of 12 months, or the corporation did not file a return for such preceding taxable year showing a liability for tax.
matchPhrases: the amount of any required installment shall be 25 percent of the required annual payment
100 percent of the tax shown on the return of the corporation for the preceding taxable year
clause (ii) shall not apply if the preceding taxable year was not a taxable year of 12 months, or the corporation did not file a return for such preceding taxable year showing a liability for tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: Required annual payment: the lesser of 100% of the current year's tax or 100% of the prior year's tax (prior year of 12 months with tax shown); each installment 25% of it.
rules.hangsApplication: Projected 2026 tax $72,844.80; 2025 tax as filed $59,302.33 for a full 12-month year. The lesser, $59,302.33, is the required annual payment: $14,825.58 an installment.

rules.issuer: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code text)

rules.question: Is HANGS a large corporation, which could not use last year's tax?
rules.whyItMatters: A large corporation may use last year's tax for its first installment only. The test is $1,000,000 of taxable income in any of the three years before.
rules.excerpt: The term "large corporation" means any corporation if such corporation (or any predecessor corporation) had taxable income of $1,000,000 or more for any taxable year during the testing period. ... The term "testing period" means the 3 taxable years immediately preceding the taxable year involved. ... the $1,000,000 amount ... shall be divided among such members [of a controlled group].
matchPhrases: if such corporation (or any predecessor corporation) had taxable income of $1,000,000 or more for any taxable year during the testing period
means the 3 taxable years immediately preceding the taxable year involved
the $1,000,000 amount specified in subparagraph (a) shall be divided among such members
taxable income shall be determined without regard to any amount carried to the taxable year under section 172 or 1212(a)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Large corporation: $1,000,000 or more of taxable income (before NOL and capital loss carryovers) in any of the 3 preceding years; a controlled group shares the $1,000,000.
rules.hangsApplication: 2023 $211,900.00, 2024 $230,000.00, 2025 $282,392.05: none near $1,000,000, no carryovers, and no controlled group (Juniper Ridge Partners LLC is a disregarded single-member LLC). The rule does not apply: last year's tax covers all four installments.
rules.sourceTitle: 26 U.S. Code 6655, Failure by corporation to pay estimated income tax
rules.issuer: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code text)

rules.question: When are a calendar-year corporation's installments due, and when may last year's tax be used?
rules.whyItMatters: The four due dates set the penalty clock; the prior-year method needs a full 12-month return with a positive tax.
rules.excerpt: Installment payments are due by the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the corporation's tax year. Example 1. Your corporation's tax year ends December 31. Installment payments are due on April 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15. ... Method 2. Each required installment is 25% of the income tax shown on the corporation's return for the previous year. ... the return must have been for a full 12 months, and the return must have shown a positive tax liability (not zero).
matchPhrases: installment payments are due by the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the corporation's tax year
your corporation's tax year ends december 31. installment payments are due on april 15, june 15, september 15, and december 15
if any due date falls on a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday, the installment is due on the next business day
each required installment is 25% of the income tax shown on the corporation's return for the previous year
the return must have been for a full 12 months, and the return must have shown a positive tax liability (not zero)
rules.pageOrSection: Estimated tax: When to pay; How to figure each required installment
rules.ruleOrLimit: Calendar year: April 15, June 15, September 15, December 15 (next business day if a weekend or holiday). Prior-year method: full 12-month prior return with positive tax.
rules.hangsApplication: 2026 dates: Wednesday April 15, Monday June 15, Tuesday September 15 and Tuesday December 15, all business days. The 2025 return was 12 months with $59,302.33 of tax.

rules.question: Is Form 1120-W still the worksheet to use?
rules.whyItMatters: The IRS retired Form 1120-W after 2022; the estimated tax worksheet now lives in Publication 542 and the Form 1120 instructions.
rules.excerpt: Form 1120-W, Estimated Tax for Corporations, and the Instructions for Form 1120-W are now historical. The 2022 Form 1120-W (released in 2021) and the 2022 Instructions for Form 1120-W (released in 2021) were the last revision of both the form and its instructions. Publication 542, Corporations, the Instructions for Form 1120 ... will be updated to include guidance on determining a corporation's estimated tax payments.
matchPhrases: form 1120-w, estimated tax for corporations, and the instructions for form 1120-w are now historical
the 2022 form 1120-w (released in 2021) and the 2022 instructions for form 1120-w (released in 2021) were the last revision of both the form and its instructions
will be updated to include guidance on determining a corporation's estimated tax payments
rules.pageOrSection: Guidance on determining a corporation's estimated tax payment
rules.ruleOrLimit: No 2026 Form 1120-W exists; use the estimated tax worksheet in Publication 542.
rules.hangsApplication: The "Form 1120-W" worksheet in this plan is the Publication 542 worksheet, line for line.

rules.question: What does the estimated tax worksheet compute?
rules.whyItMatters: Its lines are the plan's first page: expected tax, last year's tax, the smaller of the two, and 25% of it.
rules.excerpt: This worksheet may be used as a guide in figuring the required estimated tax installments. ... Enter the tax shown on the corporation's prior year's tax return. ... Enter the smaller of line 8 or line 9. ... Required installments. Enter 25% of line 10. ... Form 1120-W, Estimated Tax for Corporations, is now historical.

enter the tax shown on the corporation's prior year's tax return
enter the smaller of line 8 or line 9
required installments. enter 25% of line 10
form 1120-w, estimated tax for corporations, is now historical
rules.ruleOrLimit: Expected tax (line 8), prior-year tax (line 9), the smaller (line 10), 25% each installment (line 11), with the annualized method allowed.

rules.question: Can the slow first quarter lower the early installments?
rules.whyItMatters: If the annualized income installment is less than the regular one, the lower amount is the required installment; the reduction is recaptured in the next regular installment.
rules.excerpt: If the corporation establishes that the annualized income installment or the adjusted seasonal installment is less than the amount determined under subsection (d)(1) ... the amount of such required installment shall be the annualized income installment ... and any reduction in a required installment resulting from the application of this paragraph shall be recaptured by increasing the amount of the next required installment ... for the first 3 months of the taxable year, in the case of the 1st required installment
matchPhrases: if the corporation establishes that the annualized income installment or the adjusted seasonal installment is less than the amount determined under subsection (d)(1)
any reduction in a required installment resulting from the application of this paragraph shall be recaptured by increasing the amount of the next required installment
for the first 3 months of the taxable year, in the case of the 1st required installment
for the first 9 months of the taxable year, in the case of the 4th required installment
rules.ruleOrLimit: Each installment is the smaller of the annualized installment and the regular installment plus any reduction not yet recaptured.
rules.hangsApplication: Taxable income was $31,420.00 for the first 3 months (winter work and the January 9 bonus), so installments 1 and 2 drop to $6,598.20 each; installment 3 is $30,859.50 and installment 4 $15,246.43, which recaptures $420.84.
rules.unresolved: The interim figures are management's closed-month books, not reviewed (ANNUAL-01).

rules.question: Which annualization periods and amounts apply, and how is each installment chosen?
rules.whyItMatters: Without a Form 8842 election the standard periods (3, 3, 6 and 9 months) and amounts (4, 4, 2 and 1.33333) apply; line 38 takes the smaller of the annualized and regular-plus-recapture amounts.
rules.taxYear: 2025 instructions, the latest published; the rules come from the statute and are unchanged for 2026
rules.excerpt: Use Option 1 or Option 2 only if the corporation elected to do so by filing Form 8842 ... standard option 3 3 6 9 ... standard option 4 4 2 1.33333 ... Line 35. Enter in each column of line 35 25% of the amount from page 1, Part I, line 5. ... Line 38. For each installment, enter the smaller of line 34 or line 37 on line 38.
matchPhrases: use option 1 or option 2 only if the corporation elected to do so by filing form 8842
standard option 3 3 6 9
standard option 4 4 2 1.33333
line 35. enter in each column of line 35 25% of the amount from page 1, part i, line 5
line 38. for each installment, enter the smaller of line 34 or line 37 on line 38
rules.pageOrSection: Schedule A, Part II lines 20 and 22; Part III lines 35 and 38
rules.ruleOrLimit: Standard periods 3, 3, 6, 9 months; amounts 4, 4, 2, 1.33333; required installment the smaller of line 34 (annualized) and line 37 (regular plus recapture).
rules.hangsApplication: No Form 8842 was filed, so the standard periods apply. Line 38: $6,598.20, $6,598.20, $30,859.50, $15,246.43 = $59,302.33, the required annual payment (the 4th carries the rounding cent).

rules.question: What must go with the 2026 return if the annualized method is used, and should HANGS catch up now?
rules.whyItMatters: Using the annualized method means attaching Form 2220 even if no penalty is due; the IRS also says to catch up right away when earlier installments were short.
rules.effective: Publication 542, Estimated tax: Refiguring required installments; Form 2220.
rules.excerpt: An immediate catch-up payment should be made to reduce any penalty resulting from the underpayment of any earlier installments. ... Even if the corporation does not owe a penalty, complete and attach the form to the corporation's tax return if any of the following apply. The annualized income installment method was used to figure any required installment.
matchPhrases: an immediate catch-up payment should be made to reduce any penalty resulting from the underpayment of any earlier installments
complete and attach the form to the corporation's tax return if any of the following apply
the annualized income installment method was used to figure any required installment
rules.pageOrSection: Estimated tax: Refiguring required installments; Underpayment penalty; Form 2220
rules.ruleOrLimit: Catch up immediately on a short installment; attach Form 2220 whenever the annualized method sets an installment.
rules.hangsApplication: Installment 3 is $3,905.90 short: the plan pays it on November 13, 2026, and Form 2220 with Schedule A goes with the 2026 return.

rules.question: How long does a short installment draw the penalty, and which installment does a payment go to?
rules.whyItMatters: A payment always goes to the earliest unpaid installment, and each shortfall runs until it is paid (at the latest the 15th day of the 4th month after year end).
rules.excerpt: The penalty is figured for the period of underpayment using the underpayment rate determined under section 6621. The period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year. ... A payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains.
matchPhrases: the period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year
a payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains
the penalty is figured separately for each installment due date
rules.pageOrSection: Part IV, Figuring the Penalty; Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: Payments go to the earliest unpaid installment; each shortfall draws the underpayment rate from its due date until paid, at most to April 15, 2027.
rules.hangsApplication: April's $12,075.00 covers installment 1 and $5,476.80 of installment 2; June's covers the rest of installment 2 and $10,953.60 of installment 3; September's $16,000.00 leaves installment 3 $3,905.90 short from September 15.
rules.unresolved: June's payment counts only if the IRS moves it to 2026 (EFTPS-01).

rules.question: What underpayment rates apply in 2026?
rules.whyItMatters: The penalty is interest-like: the quarterly underpayment rate times the shortfall for each day it is unpaid.
rules.excerpt: 2026 interest rates by category ... 4th quarter (Oct-Dec) 3rd quarter (Jul-Sep) 2nd quarter (Apr-Jun) 1st quarter (Jan-Mar) ... Underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 6% 7%
matchPhrases: 2026 interest rates by category
underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 6% 7%
rules.ruleOrLimit: 2026 underpayment rate: 7% January to March, 6% April to June, 7% July to September, 7% October to December.
rules.hangsApplication: The shortfall on installment 3 runs in the third and fourth quarters at 7%: $0.75 a day on $3,905.90.
rules.unresolved: The rate for 2027 is not yet announced; the plan cures every shortfall in 2026.

rules.question: Did the rate change for October to December 2026?
rules.whyItMatters: The catch-up payment falls in the fourth quarter.
rules.excerpt: The Internal Revenue Service today announced that interest rates will remain the same for the calendar quarter beginning Oct. 1, 2026. ... 7% for underpayments (taxes owed but not fully paid).
matchPhrases: interest rates will remain the same for the calendar quarter beginning oct. 1, 2026
7% for underpayments (taxes owed but not fully paid)
rules.sourceTitle: Interest rates remain the same for the fourth quarter of 2026 (IR-2026-98)

rules.question: Which 2025 return sets the safe harbor if the 2025 return is later amended?
rules.whyItMatters: The 2025 draft carried open items; an amendment counts for the safe harbor only if filed before the installment's due date.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty.
rules.excerpt: In these instructions, "return" generally refers to the corporation's original return. However, an amended return is considered the original return if the amended return is filed by the due date (including extensions) of the original return. Also, for purposes of determining a required installment ..., if an amended return is filed for the prior tax year, then the return for the "prior tax year" includes the amended return, but only if the amended return is filed before the applicable installment due date.
matchPhrases: an amended return is considered the original return if the amended return is filed by the due date (including extensions) of the original return
then the return for the "prior tax year" includes the amended return, but only if the amended return is filed before the applicable installment due date
rules.pageOrSection: Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: The prior-year tax is the tax on the 2025 return as filed; an amendment filed later changes only the installments due after it.
rules.hangsApplication: The 2025 return was filed October 13, 2026 with $59,302.33 of tax, the Form 1120 demo's figure. An amendment before December 15 would reset the fourth installment's base (PRIOR-01).
rules.unresolved: Whether any 2025 open item (the officer pay consent, the related-party advance) will lead to an amended 2025 return before December 15 is PRIOR-01.

rules.question: How and by when must the remaining payments be made?
rules.whyItMatters: Corporate tax deposits must go by electronic funds transfer; a same-day EFTPS payment up to $1 million must be in before 3 p.m. Eastern on a business day.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), Depository Method of Tax Payment.
rules.excerpt: Corporations must use electronic funds transfer (EFT) to make all federal tax deposits (such as deposits of employment, excise, and corporate income tax). ... EFTPS accepts same day payments of $1 million or less if the payment is submitted before 3:00 p.m. Eastern time on a business day.
matchPhrases: corporations must use electronic funds transfer (eft) to make all federal tax deposits (such as deposits of employment, excise, and corporate income tax)
eftps accepts same day payments of $1 million or less if the payment is submitted before 3:00 p.m. eastern time on a business day
rules.pageOrSection: Depository Method of Tax Payment: Electronic Deposit Requirement; Depositing on Time
rules.ruleOrLimit: EFT only; EFTPS same-day payments of $1 million or less before 3:00 p.m. Eastern on a business day.
rules.hangsApplication: Two EFTPS payments, Form 1120, tax period 12/2026, estimated tax: $3,905.90 on November 13 and $15,246.43 on December 15, each scheduled ahead of its date.
rules.unresolved: A person schedules both payments; nothing has been paid (PLAN-01).

rules.question: Can the estimated tax penalty be removed for reasonable cause?
rules.whyItMatters: If it cannot, the only way to limit the penalty on the short installment is to pay it now.
rules.effective: IRS page on penalty relief for reasonable cause.
rules.excerpt: Reasonable cause is determined on a case-by-case basis considering all the facts and circumstances of your situation. ... Reasonable cause doesn't apply to certain penalties such as the estimated tax penalty.
matchPhrases: reasonable cause is determined on a case-by-case basis considering all the facts and circumstances of your situation
reasonable cause doesn't apply to certain penalties such as the estimated tax penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: Reasonable cause relief does not apply to the estimated tax penalty.
rules.hangsApplication: The $39.71 so far, and whatever accrues until the catch-up settles, stays; the plan pays the shortfall on November 13 to stop it.

excluded.why: Needs three prior years of monthly income showing a 70% seasonal pattern; HANGS works year round, so it is not tested.
Applies only to corporations with average annual adjusted financial statement income over $1 billion.
Washington has no corporate income tax; B&O tax is a separate monthly filing.

changes.note: The IRS made Form 1120-W historical after the 2022 revision. The worksheet in this plan follows the estimated tax worksheet in Publication 542.

On November 7, 2026 the IRS's Form 2220 instructions page still carried the 2025 revision; the annualization periods, amounts and the penalty rules it states come from section 6655, which is unchanged for 2026.
